title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulations on the Supervision Work of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Regulations on the Supervision Work of People's Courts

Fa Fa [2008] No. 17

All local people's courts at various levels, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic-level courts, all maritime courts, and all courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In recent years, courts at all levels have earnestly implemented the central authorities' arrangements and requirements on anti-corruption and integrity-building, highlighted key points, worked solidly, and steadily advanced various anti-corruption and integrity-building efforts, achieving notable results. At the same time, we must also clearly recognize that the struggle against corruption in people's courts currently faces a still severe situation and arduous tasks. The Interim Provisions on the Supervision Work of People's Courts, formulated and issued by our Court in 1990, can no longer fully meet the needs of strengthening internal supervision within people's courts under the new circumstances. To further improve the internal supervision mechanism of people's courts, strengthen supervision over judges and other staff members, especially supervision over leading cadres of courts, establish a long-term mechanism for anti-corruption and integrity-building in people's courts, and promote the in-depth development of supervision work in people's courts, our Court has re-formulated the Regulations on the Supervision Work of People's Courts, which are hereby issued for your earnest implementation in light of actual circumstances. Any circumstances and problems encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court.

June 5, 2008

Regulations on the Supervision Work of People's Courts

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China, the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws, and with reference to the Administrative Supervision Law of the People's Republic of China, for the purposes of strengthening the supervision work of people's courts, strictly enforcing discipline in people's courts, promoting integrity-building, and safeguarding judicial justice.

Article 2 The supervision department of a people's court is a specialized body exercising supervisory functions within the people's court, and shall, in accordance with the law and these Regulations, carry out supervision over the people's court and its judges and other staff members.

Article 3 The supervision department of a people's court shall exercise its powers in accordance with the law and these Regulations and shall not be subject to interference by administrative organs, social organizations, individuals, or other departments within the people's court.

Article 4 Supervision work in people's courts must adhere to the principle of seeking truth from facts, emphasize evidence and investigation, and ensure equality in the application of laws and discipline.

Article 5 Supervision work in people's courts shall combine education with punishment, combine strict enforcement of discipline with safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of judges and other staff members, and combine supervision and inspection with improving systems and work.

Article 6 Supervision work in people's courts shall adhere to relying on the masses. The supervision department shall establish a reporting system. Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations have the right to lodge accusations or reports with the supervision department against any violations of discipline or law by a people's court or its judges and other staff members.

Chapter II Supervision Departments and Supervision Personnel

Article 7 The Supreme People's Court and higher and intermediate people's courts shall establish Supervision Offices.

Basic-level people's courts shall establish Supervision Offices or appoint full-time supervisors.

Article 8 The Supervision Office of the Supreme People's Court shall, under the leadership of the President of the Supreme People's Court, take charge of the supervision work of courts nationwide.

The Supervision Offices of local people's courts at various levels and the full-time supervisors of basic-level people's courts shall conduct their work under the leadership of the president of their own court and the supervision department of the higher people's court, with supervision work being primarily led by the supervision department of the higher people's court.

Article 9 A Supervision Office shall have one director and, in accordance with relevant provisions, may have several deputy directors.

The director and deputy directors of a Supervision Office in a people's court at any level shall generally be selected and appointed from among judges or persons qualified to serve as judges.

The appointment and removal of the director and deputy directors of a Supervision Office in a local people's court at any level, and the full-time supervisor of a basic-level people's court, shall be subject to the consent of the supervision department of the people's court at the next higher level before the decision is submitted for approval.

Article 10 The Supervision Offices of the Supreme People's Court and higher people's courts may, based on work needs, establish internal organs responsible for handling letters and visits and reports, case investigation, supervision and inspection, comprehensive research, and other work. Intermediate people's courts and lower may establish such organs by reference based on actual circumstances.

Article 11 The Supervision Office of the Supreme People's Court, higher people's courts, and intermediate people's courts in sub-provincial cities shall have supervisors and supervision officers; intermediate people's courts and basic-level people's courts shall have supervision officers in their Supervision Offices.

People's courts at all levels shall, to the extent possible, select and appoint judges or persons qualified to serve as judges to serve as supervisors and supervision officers.

People's courts may appoint part-time supervision officers from departments other than the court's own supervision department, and the part-time supervision work they perform shall be under the leadership of the supervision department of the court where they work.

Article 12 Supervision personnel must be loyal to their duties, enforce discipline impartially, abide by laws and discipline, and maintain confidentiality.

Article 13 Any supervision personnel who abuses power, engages in malpractices for personal gain, neglects duties, or leaks secrets shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions; if the conduct constitutes a crime, the matter shall be transferred to the relevant authorities for legal handling.

Chapter III Functions and Duties of Supervision Departments

Article 14 The main functions and duties of the supervision department of a people's court are:

(1) To inspect the compliance with and implementation of national laws and regulations by the people's court and its judges and other staff members;

(2) To formulate and improve the integrity system of the people's court, and to inspect the implementation of the integrity system by the people's court and its judges and other staff members;

(3) To accept accusations and reports against the people's court and its judges and other staff members for violations of discipline or law;

(4) To investigate and handle acts by the people's court and its judges and other staff members that violate trial discipline, enforcement discipline, or other discipline;

(5) To accept applications for reconsideration and appeals by judges and other staff members who are dissatisfied with disciplinary sanctions;

(6) To organize coordination, inspect and guide the correction of unhealthy practices that harm the interests of the masses in trial work, enforcement work, and other work of the court;

(7) To organize coordination, inspect and guide the prevention of corruption, and carry out education for judges and other staff members on judicial integrity and compliance with laws and discipline.

Article 15 The Supervision Office of the Supreme People's Court shall carry out supervision over the following units, departments, and persons:

(1) All departments of the Supreme People's Court and their judges and other staff members;

(2) Higher people's courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and their presidents, vice presidents, leading cadres at the vice-presidential level, and directors of Supervision Offices.

Article 16 The Supervision Offices of higher people's courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and intermediate people's courts, shall carry out supervision over the following units, departments, and persons:

(1) All departments of the court and their judges and other staff members;

(2) The people's court at the next lower level, and its president, vice presidents, leading cadres at the vice-presidential level, director of the Supervision Office, and full-time supervisor.

Article 17 The Supervision Office or full-time supervisor of a basic-level people's court shall carry out supervision over all departments of the court and their judges and other staff members.

Article 18 The supervision department of a higher people's court may handle supervisory matters within the jurisdiction of the supervision department of the people's court at the next lower level; when necessary, it may handle supervisory matters within the jurisdiction of the supervision departments of all lower people's courts under its jurisdiction.

Chapter IV Powers of Supervision Departments

Article 19 In performing their duties, supervision departments have the power to require the units, departments, and persons under supervision to provide documents, materials, case files, financial accounts, and other relevant materials related to the supervisory matter, and to inspect or make copies thereof; to require the units, departments, and persons under supervision to provide explanations or clarifications on issues involved in the supervisory matter; and to order the units, departments, and persons under supervision to cease any acts that violate laws, regulations, and discipline.

Article 20 When investigating acts that violate laws, regulations, and discipline, supervision departments may, based on the actual circumstances, take the following measures:

(1) Temporarily seize or seal up documents, materials, financial accounts, case materials, and other relevant materials of the units, departments, and persons involved in the case that may prove violations of laws, regulations, and discipline;

(2) Order the units, departments, and persons involved in the case not to sell, transfer, or destroy property related to the case during the investigation period;

(3) With the approval of the supervision department of the people's court at the next higher level, order a person suspected of violating discipline to provide explanations and clarifications on issues involved in the investigation at a designated time and place, but may not detain such person or impose disguised detention;

(4) Recommend the suspension of official duties of a person seriously suspected of violating discipline;

(5) Upon approval, inquire into the deposits of the units and persons involved in the case in banks or other financial institutions, and when necessary, may take preservation measures in accordance with the law to freeze the deposits of the persons involved in the case in banks or other financial institutions;

(6) Conduct inquiries to the units, departments, and persons involved in the supervisory matter;

(7) Attend meetings of the unit or department under supervision that are related to the supervisory matter.

When taking the measures specified in subparagraphs (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) of the preceding paragraph, a notice of supervision shall be prepared and served on the relevant units, departments, and persons, and a list of the relevant property shall be made.

Article 21 Based on the results of inspections or investigations, supervision departments may make supervision recommendations in any of the following circumstances:

(1) Where there is a refusal to implement laws or regulations, or a violation of laws, regulations, or the discipline of the people's court, which should be corrected;

(2) Where there is a violation of the discipline of the people's court, which should result in a disciplinary sanction of warning, demerit, major demerit, demotion, removal from office, or dismissal;

(3) Where a decision on recruitment, appointment or removal, or reward or punishment is clearly inappropriate and should be corrected;

(4) Where there is a need to improve systems and plug loopholes;

(5) Other circumstances where a supervision recommendation is necessary.

Article 22 Supervision recommendations shall be issued in the name of the people's court and served in writing on the relevant units, departments, and persons.

Important supervision recommendations shall be reported to the supervision department of the people's court at the next higher level for filing.

The units, departments, and persons to which a supervision recommendation is addressed shall adopt the recommendation unless there is a justifiable reason; if there is an objection to the supervision recommendation, a written objection shall be submitted to the people's court that made the recommendation within 30 days from the date of receipt of the supervision recommendation. The supervision department shall respond within 30 days from the date of receipt of the objection.

Article 23 Based on the results of inspections or investigations, if a disciplinary sanction should be imposed on a person who violates the discipline of the people's court, the supervision department shall, in accordance with the procedures for disciplinary sanctions, propose a disciplinary sanction opinion or make a supervision recommendation.

Chapter V Supervision Procedures

Article 24 Supervision departments shall conduct inspections in accordance with the following procedures:

(1) Determine the inspection matter based on the instructions or requirements of the president of the court or the supervision department of the higher people's court;

(2) Formulate an inspection plan and organize its implementation; when necessary, may arrange for relevant departments of the court or lower people's courts to participate in the inspection;

(3) Report the inspection results to the president of the court or the supervision department of the higher people's court;

(4) Based on the inspection results, propose a disciplinary sanction opinion or a supervision recommendation.

Article 25 Within the scope of jurisdiction, based on problems discovered during inspections, or clues of disciplinary violations from accusations or reports, or clues of disciplinary violations transferred by relevant organs or departments, after preliminary verification, if it is found that a person has committed a disciplinary violation and should be subject to a disciplinary sanction, the supervision department shall report to the president of the court for approval, file a case, and organize an investigation.

Filing of important cases shall be reported to the supervision department of the people's court at the next higher level for filing.

Article 26 When investigating disciplinary cases, the supervision department of a people's court shall form a case investigation group and a case review group to conduct the case investigation and case review separately. Persons participating in the case investigation shall not participate in the case review.

If the personnel of the supervision department are insufficient to form a case investigation group and a case review group, the supervision department may, with the approval of the president of the court, designate part-time supervision officers of the court to participate in the case investigation and case review.

Article 27 When investigating a disciplinary case, the supervision department shall comprehensively collect evidence and hear the statements and defenses of the person under investigation.

Article 28 If a supervision officer has an interest in the supervisory matter being handled, or has any other relationship that may affect the impartial handling of the case, such supervision officer shall withdraw.

Article 29 A case filed by the supervision department for investigation shall be concluded within six months from the date of filing. If an extension of time is necessary due to special reasons, the time limit may be appropriately extended, but the matter shall be reported to the supervision department of the people's court at the next higher level for filing, with an explanation of the circumstances and reasons.

Article 30 If, after investigation of a filed case, it is determined that no disciplinary violation exists, or the circumstances are minor and do not warrant a disciplinary sanction, the case shall be dismissed in accordance with the procedures for approval of filing, and the person under investigation shall be notified.

Article 31 For a case in which a disciplinary sanction may be imposed, after the investigation group concludes its investigation, the case shall be referred to the review group for review.

Article 32 Case review shall be conducted in the form of a hearing or a written review. When conducting a written review, the person under investigation shall be questioned and given the opportunity to make statements and defenses; when necessary, the testimony may also be corroborated with witnesses.

Article 33 Disciplinary sanctions against a person who violates discipline shall be imposed in accordance with the following provisions:

(1) For a member of the Judicial Committee of the court, a division president, a division vice president, a judge, an assistant judge, or other staff member of the court, or the president, vice president, leading cadre at the vice-presidential level, director of the Supervision Office, or full-time supervisor of the people's court at the next lower level, if it is proposed to impose a warning, demerit, or major demerit sanction, the supervision department shall propose a sanction opinion, report to the president of the court for approval, and then issue the disciplinary sanction decision; if it is proposed to impose a demotion, removal from office, or dismissal sanction, the supervision department shall propose a sanction opinion, and after approval by the meeting of the president of the court, issue the disciplinary sanction decision. The disciplinary sanction decision shall be issued in the name of the people's court and affixed with the seal of the people's court.

(2) If a disciplinary sanction of removal from office or dismissal is to be imposed on a person who violates discipline, and it is necessary first to request the people's congress at the same level or its standing committee to recall the person from office, or to remove or dismiss the person from office, the sanction decision shall be executed only after the person's recall, removal, or dismissal by the people's congress or its standing committee.

Article 34 After a disciplinary sanction is imposed on a person who violates discipline, the personnel department of the relevant people's court shall handle the sanction procedures, and materials such as the disciplinary sanction decision shall be placed in the file of the sanctioned person.

Article 35 If a person subject to a disciplinary sanction is dissatisfied with the decision, the person may, within 30 days from the date of receipt of the disciplinary sanction decision, apply for reconsideration to the people's court that made the decision; the reconsidering people's court shall make a reconsideration decision within 30 days. If still dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, the person may, within 30 days from the receipt of the reconsideration decision, appeal to the people's court at the next higher level that made the reconsideration decision; the people's court at the next higher level shall make a handling decision within 60 days.

During the period of reconsideration and appeal, the execution of the original decision shall not be suspended.

Article 36 If, upon review of an appeal against a disciplinary sanction decision, the people's court at the next higher level finds that the original decision is inappropriate, it may recommend that the people's court that made the original disciplinary sanction decision modify or revoke the decision; it may also directly make a decision to modify or revoke the decision in accordance with the procedures for disciplinary sanctions.

The handling decision of the people's court at the next higher level on the appeal shall be final.

Article 37 Where there are other provisions on the authority and procedures for disciplinary sanctions against judges, those provisions shall apply.

Article 38 For a reporter who deliberately fabricates facts and falsely accuses a court staff member, a recommendation shall be made to the relevant unit for handling; if the conduct constitutes a crime, the matter shall be transferred to the relevant authorities in accordance with the law for criminal liability.

Article 39 If a unit, department, or person under supervision violates these Regulations in any of the following ways, the supervision department shall order rectification; if rectification is refused, the responsible person shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions in accordance with discipline:

(1) Concealing the truth, producing false evidence, or hiding, transferring, altering, or destroying evidence;

(2) Deliberately delaying or refusing to provide documents, materials, financial accounts, or other relevant materials and other necessary information related to the supervisory matter;

(3) Selling or transferring property involved in the case during the investigation period;

(4) Refusing to provide explanations or clarifications on questions raised by the supervision department;

(5) Refusing to execute a disciplinary sanction decision or, without justifiable reason, refusing to adopt a supervision recommendation;

(6) Other acts in violation of these Regulations, where the circumstances are serious.

Chapter VI Supplementary Provisions

Article 40 The term "leading cadres at the vice-presidential level" as used in these Regulations refers to the Director of the Political Department (Director of the Political Affairs Division, Head of the Political Work Section) of a local people's court, or full-time members of the Judicial Committee in a leading position, the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau, and other such persons.

Article 41 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 42 These Regulations shall come into effect as of the date of issuance, and the Interim Provisions on the Supervision Work of People's Courts shall be simultaneously abolished.
